text: Overall, how have you been feeling generally in terms of your energy levels, unexplained weight changes, or daily well-being?
rationale: Routine primary care constitutional screening question.

text: Have you experienced any fever, chills, persistent fatigue, or drenching night sweats?
rationale: Screening for systemic infection, occult inflammatory condition, or malignancy.

text: Have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as pain, burning, increased frequency, trouble starting your stream, or discoloration?
rationale: General review of systems screening for genitourinary abnormalities.

text: When did your urinary symptoms first start, and did they come on suddenly or develop gradually?
rationale: Clarifies acute versus chronic timeline for urinary presentation.

text: How much do these urinary symptoms interfere with your daily life or disrupt your sleep at night?
rationale: Assesses clinical severity and quality-of-life impact.

text: Have you experienced any persistent cough, shortness of breath, wheezing, or chest congestion?
rationale: Primary pulmonology review of systems screening.

text: When did your breathing difficulty or cough first begin, and did it follow a cold or respiratory infection?
rationale: Differentiates acute viral/post-infectious etiology from subacute or chronic lung disease.

text: On a scale of 1 to 10, how significantly is your breathing limiting your physical activity today?
rationale: Quantifies functional impairment from respiratory symptoms.

text: Have you felt any chest discomfort, tightness, heart fluttering, rapid heartbeat, or swelling in your ankles?
rationale: Primary cardiovascular review of systems screening.

text: When did this chest discomfort, heart fluttering, or swelling first begin, and has it become more frequent?
rationale: Establishes symptom trajectory in cardiovascular disease.

text: On a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is the chest discomfort or shortness of breath at its worst?
rationale: Standard OPQRST clinical quantification of cardiovascular distress.

text: Have you had any stomach pain, acid reflux, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, or changes in your bowel habits?
rationale: Primary gastrointestinal review of systems screening.

text: When did this digestive or stomach issue begin, and does it come and go in waves or stay constant?
rationale: Clarifies colic versus constant inflammatory gastrointestinal presentation.

text: On a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is your abdominal discomfort at its worst point today?
rationale: Standard clinical pain severity scale for abdominal symptoms.

text: Have you experienced any persistent headaches, dizziness, numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arms or legs?
rationale: Primary neurologic review of systems screening.

text: When did this nerve, headache, or weakness symptom begin, and is it getting steadily worse, improving, or fluctuating?
rationale: Determines temporal dynamic of neurologic presentation.

text: On a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is this neurological symptom or headache at its worst?
rationale: Quantifies severity of neurologic presentation.

text: Have you experienced any joint pain, stiffness, back pain, or muscle aches?
rationale: Primary musculoskeletal and rheumatologic review of systems screening.

text: When did this joint, muscle, or back pain start, and was there a specific injury, fall, or twist that triggered it?
rationale: Differentiates acute traumatic injury from insidious inflammatory or degenerative arthropathy.

text: On a scale from 1 to 10, how would you rate your muscle, joint, or back pain today?
rationale: Standard numerical rating scale for musculoskeletal pain.

text: Have you noticed any changes in your vision, eye pain, redness, or sensitivity to light?
rationale: Primary ophthalmology review of systems screening.

text: When did this eye discomfort or vision change begin, and is it affecting one eye or both eyes?
rationale: Determines laterality and acute versus chronic ophthalmic timeline.

text: Have you had any toothaches, bleeding gums, jaw discomfort, or mouth sores?
rationale: Primary oral and dental health screening.

text: When did this tooth, gum, or mouth pain begin, and have you had dental work done recently?
rationale: Clarifies acute odontogenic versus chronic oral mucosal timeline.

text: Have you noticed any new or changing skin rashes, unusual moles, severe itching, or non-healing sores?
rationale: Primary dermatologic review of systems screening.

text: When did this rash or skin lesion first appear, and has it spread to other areas of your body?
rationale: Differentiates acute exanthem from localized chronic dermatosis.

text: Have you experienced excessive thirst, unexplained weight changes, or unusual sensitivity to cold or heat?
rationale: Primary endocrine and metabolic screening for diabetes and thyroid disorders.

text: Have you noticed unusual bleeding, easy bruising, swollen lymph glands, or persistent pale skin?
rationale: Primary hematologic screening for cytopenias, coagulopathy, and lymphadenopathy.

text: Have you had any high fevers, recent international travel, tick bites, or exposure to anyone with serious infectious illnesses?
rationale: Epidemiological infectious disease risk screening.

text: Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling unusually down, anxious, or overwhelmed by stress?
rationale: Validated preliminary screening for mood and anxiety symptoms.

text: How would you describe your typical daily diet, water intake, and sleep schedule?
rationale: Baseline lifestyle, nutritional, and hydration assessment.

text: Do you currently smoke cigarettes, use vape or tobacco products, drink alcohol, or have toxic exposures at work?
rationale: Standard social history and risk factor screening.

text: Has anyone in your immediate family been diagnosed with serious conditions such as early heart disease, cancer, diabetes, or kidney disorders?
rationale: Primary familial disease predisposition screening.

text: Are you completely unable to pass urine despite having a full, painful, distended bladder?
rationale: Emergency red flag for acute urinary retention requiring urgent decompression.

text: Have you noticed bright red blood, large dark clots, or frank blood throughout your urine stream?
rationale: Emergency screen for gross hematuria requiring cystoscopy to rule out urothelial malignancy.

text: Do you have high fevers, shaking chills, and flank pain together with burning or difficulty passing urine?
rationale: Emergency screen for acute pyelonephritis and urosepsis.

text: Do you have new numbness in your saddle area (groin/buttocks), leg weakness, or loss of bowel control with urinary issues?
rationale: Emergency screen for Cauda Equina Syndrome requiring immediate neurosurgical decompression.

text: Have you produced zero or almost zero urine for the past 12 to 24 hours?
rationale: Emergency indicator for acute renal failure or bilateral ureteral obstruction.

text: Did severe, excruciating pain in the testicle or scrotum start suddenly within the last few hours?
rationale: Emergency screen for testicular torsion requiring surgical exploration within 6 hours.

text: Are you struggling to breathe, gasping, or unable to speak more than a couple words at a time?
rationale: Emergency red flag for acute respiratory failure requiring immediate oxygenation and airway triage.

text: Are you coughing up bright red blood, blood clots, or more than a teaspoon of pure blood?
rationale: Emergency screen for massive hemoptysis from cavitary disease, PE, or vascular rupture.

text: Is your throat swelling shut or making high-pitched squeaking sounds when breathing in?
rationale: Emergency upper airway obstruction requiring immediate airway protection.

text: Have your lips, tongue, or fingertips turned blue, purple, or pale gray?
rationale: Direct physical sign of severe arterial hypoxemia and cyanosis.

text: Did sharp chest pain and sudden severe breathlessness strike instantaneously like a bolt of lightning?
rationale: Classic presentation of acute massive pulmonary embolism or spontaneous tension pneumothorax.

text: Is your chest pain crushing, heavy, or accompanied by cold drenching sweats, nausea, and severe breathlessness?
rationale: Emergency screen for Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI/NSTEMI) requiring immediate 911 activation.

text: Did severe, excruciating pain tear or rip through from your chest directly into the center of your back between the shoulder blades?
rationale: Pathognomonic presentation of acute aortic dissection requiring immediate vascular imaging.

text: Did you pass out or faint suddenly right in the middle of strenuous physical exertion?
rationale: Dangerous presentation of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, critical aortic stenosis, or malignant ventricular arrhythmia.

text: Are you coughing up pink frothy fluid while gasping for air and unable to lie flat?
rationale: Emergency presentation of acute decompensated heart failure with flash pulmonary edema.

text: Are you vomiting bright red blood, large dark clots, or dark coffee-ground material?
rationale: Emergency screen for massive upper GI bleeding from bleeding ulcer, Mallory-Weiss tear, or esophageal varices.

text: Is your belly rock-hard, board-like, and agonizingly painful with any slight movement or bump of the bed?
rationale: Emergency physical sign of acute peritonitis from visceral perforation (ruptured ulcer, appendix, diverticulum).

text: Have you stopped passing both gas and bowel movements completely while your belly swells and you vomit?
rationale: Emergency screen for complete mechanical bowel obstruction requiring surgical decompression.

text: Are you passing large volumes of pure red blood or maroon clots from your rectum accompanied by weakness or fainting?
rationale: Emergency lower GI hemorrhage requiring urgent resuscitation and endoscopic intervention.

text: Do you have sudden facial drooping, arm weakness, or slurred/incoherent speech that began within the last 4.5 hours?
rationale: Emergency stroke alert (FAST protocol) within the critical tPA thrombolysis window.

text: Did the worst headache of your entire life strike instantaneously like a clap of thunder?
rationale: Emergency screen for ruptured cerebral aneurysm and subarachnoid hemorrhage.

text: Do you have high fever, confusion, neck stiffness, and a dark purple non-blanching rash on your skin?
rationale: Emergency screen for acute meningococcal meningitis and purpura fulminans.

text: Has a seizure lasted longer than 5 minutes, or have multiple seizures occurred without waking up in between?
rationale: Emergency status epilepticus requiring immediate parenteral anticonvulsant therapy.

text: Is weakness or numbness rapidly spreading upwards from your feet into your legs, hips, and chest?
rationale: Emergency screen for Guillain-Barre syndrome with impending diaphragmatic paralysis.

text: Did painless vision loss go completely black in one eye within seconds (like a shade being pulled down)?
rationale: Emergency screen for Central Retinal Artery Occlusion (CRAO) or Giant Cell Arteritis.

text: Is your eye intensely red and painful, cloudy, and does the eyeball feel as hard as a marble?
rationale: Emergency screen for Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma requiring immediate pressure-lowering drops.

text: Did a chemical or alkaline cleaning solution just splash directly into your eye?
rationale: Immediate true ocular emergency: requires instant continuous eye wash.

text: Is a dark curtain or shadow rapidly expanding across your vision with bright lightning flashes?
rationale: Emergency screen for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment requiring immediate laser or surgical repair.

text: Is your neck or the floor of your mouth under your tongue rapidly swelling, pushing your tongue up and making breathing hard?
rationale: Life-threatening Ludwig's Angina emergency with impending airway closure.

text: Is facial swelling rapidly closing your eye or spreading up toward your temple and bridge of your nose?
rationale: Risk of cavernous sinus thrombosis from retrograde orbital venous spread.

text: Is a single joint (like your knee or hip) excruciatingly painful, hot, bright red, and completely impossible to bend or bear weight on, with fever?
rationale: Emergency screen for acute septic arthritis requiring immediate joint aspiration.

text: Does your injured leg or arm have severe, agonizing pain out of proportion to the injury, with severe tightness and numbness in your toes/fingers?
rationale: Emergency screen for acute compartment syndrome requiring immediate fasciotomy.

text: Has a broken bone punctured or torn through the surface of your skin?
rationale: Emergency screen for open fracture requiring urgent orthopedic irrigation, debridement, and IV antibiotics.

text: Is an area of red swollen skin developing severe pain far out of proportion to its appearance, with purplish blisters or crackling beneath the skin?
rationale: Emergency screen for necrotizing soft tissue infection (flesh-eating disease).

text: Are your lips, mouth, eyes, or genitals peeling and blistering with painful sheets of skin sloughing off?
rationale: Emergency screen for Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis.

text: Do you have rapid deep breathing, fruity-smelling breath, persistent vomiting, and extreme confusion?
rationale: Emergency screen for Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA).

text: Do you have extreme restlessness, delirium, high fever over 103°F, and a heart rate pounding over 140 beats per minute?
rationale: Emergency screen for life-threatening thyroid storm.

text: Do you have severe dizziness, fainting, profound weakness, vomiting, and dangerously low blood pressure?
rationale: Emergency screen for acute adrenal crisis in known or suspected adrenal insufficiency.

text: Are you having spontaneous bleeding from your gums and nose with hundreds of tiny pinpoint purple spots (petechiae) covering your legs?
rationale: Emergency screen for severe immune thrombocytopenia or acute leukemia.

text: Are you currently receiving chemotherapy for cancer and have a new fever of 100.4°F (38.0°C) or higher?
rationale: Emergency screen for neutropenic fever requiring immediate broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour.

text: Do you feel severely ill with confusion, rapid shallow breathing, clammy mottled skin, and inability to stay awake?
rationale: Emergency screen for systemic sepsis and septic shock.

text: Are your lips and tongue swelling shut with hives and trouble breathing after eating a food, taking medicine, or getting a bug sting?
rationale: Life-threatening anaphylaxis requiring immediate intramuscular epinephrine.

text: Do you have active thoughts of ending your life right now, or do you have a specific plan and access to lethal means?
rationale: Emergency psychiatric crisis safety screen requiring immediate crisis intervention and emergency evaluation.

text: Are you hearing voices commanding you to harm yourself or someone else?
rationale: Emergency psychiatric evaluation for command hallucinations.

text: What are the names and dosages of all prescription medications you currently take on a daily or regular basis?
rationale: Comprehensive medication reconciliation to identify drug interactions and adherence.

text: Do you take any blood thinners such as warfarin, Eliquis, Xarelto, Plavix, or daily baby aspirin?
rationale: Critical anticoagulation status for bleeding risk.

text: Do you take blood pressure medications like lisinopril, amlodipine, losartan, or hydrochlorothiazide?
rationale: Documents hypertension treatment regimen.

text: Do you use insulin injections, metformin, or other medications for blood sugar control?
rationale: Documents glycemic management regimen.

text: How often do you take over-the-counter pain medications like ibuprofen (Advil/Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or acetaminophen (Tylenol)?
rationale: Screens for NSAID-induced gastritis, ulcers, and acute kidney injury.

text: Do you take any vitamins, herbal remedies, bodybuilding powders, or dietary supplements?
rationale: Identifies herbal supplement hepatotoxicity and drug-herb interactions.

text: Have you ever had an allergic reaction, hives, or swelling from penicillin, amoxicillin, or other antibiotics?
rationale: Vital antibiotic allergy history.

text: Are you allergic to sulfa medications like Bactrim/Septra?
rationale: Identifies sulfonamide hypersensitivity.

text: Have you had an allergic reaction to IV radiocontrast dye used for CT scans?
rationale: Critical pre-imaging contrast safety assessment.

text: Do you have allergies to latex rubber, medical tape adhesives, or iodine prep solutions?
rationale: Procedural and physical contact allergy safety.

text: Do you have severe food allergies to peanuts, tree nuts, shellfish, eggs, or wheat that require an EpiPen?
rationale: Identifies high-risk food anaphylaxis history.

text: Have you had any abdominal surgeries such as gallbladder removal, appendix removal, hernia repair, or bowel surgery?
rationale: Evaluates baseline surgical anatomy and risk for postoperative adhesions.

text: Have you had pelvic surgery such as prostatectomy, hysterectomy, C-section, or bladder sling?
rationale: Evaluates surgical etiology for urinary dysfunction or pelvic organ prolapse.

text: Have you ever had heart surgery, coronary stents placed, balloon angioplasty, or a pacemaker implanted?
rationale: Establishes documented structural or ischemic heart disease.

text: Have you had total knee, hip, or shoulder joint replacements, or spinal fusion surgery?
rationale: Evaluates prosthetic joint infection risks and orthopedic baseline.

text: Have you or any blood relative ever had a severe fever, delayed waking, or complication with general anesthesia (malignant hyperthermia)?
rationale: Critical surgical and anesthesia safety assessment.

text: Have you been admitted overnight to a hospital or intensive care unit in the past two years, and for what reason?
rationale: Quantifies disease severity and baseline medical frailty.

text: Have you ever received a blood transfusion, and did you have any allergic reaction to the blood?
rationale: Establishes prior severe anemia or hemorrhage and alloimmunization.

text: Have you ever been diagnosed with cancer or received chemotherapy or radiation therapy?
rationale: Critical oncologic history informing immunosuppression and secondary malignancy risks.

text: When did you receive your most recent tetanus booster shot (Td or Tdap): was it within the past 10 years?
rationale: Screens for tetanus prophylaxis needs in wounds or routine care.

text: Are you up-to-date on your annual flu shot, COVID-19 booster, and shingles or pneumonia vaccines if eligible?
rationale: Standard adult immunization audit.

text: If applicable, when was your most recent screening mammogram, and were the results normal?
rationale: Standard breast cancer screening quality metric.

text: If applicable, when was your last Pap smear and HPV test for cervical cancer screening?
rationale: Standard cervical cancer screening compliance.

text: Have you had a colonoscopy or stool test for colorectal cancer screening in the past 5 to 10 years?
rationale: Colorectal cancer screening adherence.

text: Have you had a bone density (DEXA) scan to check for osteoporosis or thinning bones?
rationale: Screens for osteoporotic fracture risk in older adults.

text: When did you last see an optometrist or ophthalmologist for a comprehensive dilated eye exam?
rationale: Routine preventive vision and glaucoma screening.

text: When was your last routine dental cleaning and dental checkup with bitewing x-rays?
rationale: Routine oral health maintenance assessment.

text: Can you walk independently around your home without using a cane, walker, or wheelchair?
rationale: Basic functional mobility assessment (ADL).

text: Do you need physical assistance from another person to take a shower, dress yourself, or use the toilet?
rationale: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) dependence assessment.

text: Are you able to prepare your own meals, manage your medications, and handle your finances independently?
rationale: Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) independence.

text: How many times have you fallen or lost your balance in the past 12 months?
rationale: Validated geriatric fall risk screening question.

text: Have you ever required a Foley catheter, self-catheterization, or nephrostomy tube?
rationale: Assesses prior invasive urinary instrumentation.

text: Approximately how many confirmed urinary infections have you had over your adult lifetime?
rationale: Quantifies chronic recurrent genitourinary infection burden.

text: If applicable, what was your most recent PSA (Prostate-Specific Antigen) blood test result?
rationale: Documents prostatic biomarker status.

text: Have you ever had a kidney ultrasound or CT scan of your kidneys and bladder?
rationale: Documents prior structural renal imaging findings.

text: Have you ever performed a spirometry or pulmonary function test (blowing into a tube)?
rationale: Objective documentation of obstructive or restrictive lung defect.

text: Do you use supplemental oxygen at home, either with a nasal cannula or oxygen concentrator?
rationale: Identifies chronic respiratory failure and hypoxemia.

text: Have you been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea, and do you use a CPAP mask at night?
rationale: Assesses sleep-disordered breathing and cardiovascular risk.

text: How many times in your life have you been diagnosed with pneumonia requiring antibiotics?
rationale: Identifies recurrent lower respiratory infection susceptibility.

text: Have you ever had an ultrasound of your heart (echocardiogram), and do you know your ejection fraction?
rationale: Assesses left ventricular systolic function.

text: Have you ever taken a treadmill stress test or nuclear cardiac scan to check blood flow to your heart?
rationale: Identifies documented inducible myocardial ischemia.

text: What is your typical systolic (top number) blood pressure when measured at home?
rationale: Assesses home blood pressure control.

text: Have you ever worn a 24-hour or 14-day Holter heart monitor patch for palpitations?
rationale: Documents prior ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring.

text: Have you ever had an upper endoscopy (EGD) where a doctor placed a camera down into your stomach?
rationale: Identifies known Barrett's esophagus, peptic ulcer, or gastritis.

text: Have you ever been tested or treated with antibiotic triple therapy for Helicobacter pylori stomach bacteria?
rationale: Documents prior peptic disease risk factors.

text: Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C virus infection?
rationale: Assesses viral hepatitis and cirrhosis risk.

text: Have you ever had an ultrasound showing gallstones or sludge in your gallbladder?
rationale: Documents cholelithiasis history.

text: Have you had an MRI or CT scan of your brain in the past, and what were the main findings?
rationale: Documents prior neuroimaging abnormalities.

text: How many concussions or head injuries with loss of consciousness have you experienced in your life?
rationale: Quantifies traumatic brain injury burden.

text: Have you had an EMG or nerve conduction study done on your hands, arms, or legs for numbness?
rationale: Objective electrodiagnostic documentation of neuropathy.

text: How many bone fractures or broken bones have you had during your adult life?
rationale: Assesses skeletal fragility and osteopenia/osteoporosis.

text: Have you received cortisone, steroid, or gel injections into any of your knees, hips, or shoulders?
rationale: Documents prior conservative interventional orthopedic therapies.

text: Have you completed formal physical therapy for your neck, back, or joint problems in the past year?
rationale: Evaluates conservative rehabilitation compliance.

text: If you have diabetes or prediabetes, what was your most recent Hemoglobin A1c percentage?
rationale: Standard 3-month glycemic control metric.

text: What was your most recent TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) lab test result: normal, high, or low?
rationale: Assesses biochemical thyroid status.

text: Have you been diagnosed with vitamin D deficiency, and do you take weekly or daily vitamin D supplements?
rationale: Screens for metabolic bone disease and hypovitaminosis D.

text: When did a dermatologist last perform a full-body skin exam checking all your moles and spots?
rationale: Annual melanoma surveillance compliance.

text: Have you ever had a skin spot biopsied that turned out to be melanoma, basal cell, or squamous cell skin cancer?
rationale: Personal history of cutaneous malignancy.

text: Have you ever been told by an eye doctor that the pressure inside your eye (intraocular pressure) is high?
rationale: Screens for ocular hypertension and glaucoma risk.

text: Have you been diagnosed with cataracts, or have you had cataract extraction surgery with lens replacement?
rationale: Documents crystalline lens status.

text: When did you last have a full mouth series or panoramic x-ray of all your teeth and jawbones?
rationale: Periodontal and periapical radiographic surveillance.

text: Do you brush with fluoridated toothpaste twice daily, and do you drink fluoridated municipal water?
rationale: Baseline dental caries preventive exposure.

text: Have you ever been told you are anemic or have low iron, requiring iron pills or iron infusions?
rationale: Documents chronic microcytic or normocytic anemia history.

text: Have you personally ever had a DVT (deep vein clot in your leg) or PE (pulmonary clot in your lungs)?
rationale: Direct personal history of venous thromboembolism.

text: Have you ever had a positive PPD skin test or positive QuantiFERON blood test for latent tuberculosis?
rationale: Documents prior Mycobacterium tuberculosis exposure.

text: How many confirmed times have you had COVID-19, and did you develop any long-term symptoms?
rationale: Quantifies post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC).

text: Is your urine stream visibly weaker, slower, or thinner than it used to be?
rationale: Peak flow reduction characteristic of bladder outlet obstruction.

text: Do you have to wait several seconds or minutes at the toilet before your urine stream starts to flow?
rationale: Urinary hesitancy diagnostic of prostatic enlargement or stricture.

text: Do you find yourself bearing down, straining, or pushing with your abdominal muscles to pass urine?
rationale: Screens for high voiding pressure and mechanical obstruction.

text: Does your urine stream stop and restart multiple times during a single trip to the bathroom?
rationale: Interrupted voiding from detrusor underactivity or mechanical obstruction.

text: Do you experience prolonged dribbling of urine onto your clothing right after you feel finished voiding?
rationale: Post-micturition dribble common in urethral pooling and BPH.

text: Do you have the persistent feeling that your bladder is still partly full immediately after urinating?
rationale: Evaluates post-void residual sensation and chronic urinary retention.

text: Do you feel the need to urinate again within 10 to 15 minutes of having just emptied your bladder?
rationale: Identifies incomplete bladder emptying and high post-void residuals.

text: Does your urine stream split into two, spray, or fan out rather than forming a single stream?
rationale: Screens for urethral meatal stenosis or distal stricture disease.

text: Do you find it noticeably easier to pass urine while sitting down compared to standing up?
rationale: Common behavioral adaptation in men with prostatic obstruction.

text: Do you ever have to press on your lower abdomen or perineum to help push the remaining urine out?
rationale: Identifies severe retention or urethral diverticulum.

text: Approximately how many times do you urinate during your typical waking hours?
rationale: Quantifies daytime urinary frequency (normal is 4-7 times daily).

text: How many times each night do you wake up specifically because you need to urinate?
rationale: Quantifies nocturia (>=2 episodes is clinically significant).

text: Do you get sudden, compelling urges to urinate that feel almost impossible to postpone?
rationale: Identifies detrusor overactivity and bladder sensory urgency.

text: When you feel that sudden strong urge, do you ever leak urine before you can reach the toilet?
rationale: Differentiates urge incontinence (OAB wet) from dry urgency.

text: Do you leak small drops of urine when coughing, sneezing, laughing, lifting heavy objects, or exercising?
rationale: Identifies stress urinary incontinence from pelvic floor laxity.

text: Do you leak both with physical exertion like coughing AND when you have a sudden intense urge?
rationale: Distinguishes mixed urinary incontinence requiring multimodal therapy.

text: Does urine ever leak out continuously or without you feeling any urge or sensation beforehand?
rationale: Screens for continuous overflow incontinence, fistulas, or severe sphincter deficit.

text: Have you ever wet the bed while asleep during the night as an adult?
rationale: High-risk indicator for severe bladder compliance loss or overflow retention.

text: Do you currently wear absorbent pads or liners for bladder leaks, and if so, how many pads do you soak per day?
rationale: Objective clinical metric for quantifying incontinence severity.

text: Do your frequent trips to the bathroom happen mostly after drinking coffee, tea, alcohol, or large volumes of water?
rationale: Identifies dietary bladder irritants and polydipsia.

text: Does the burning sensation happen primarily at the initial start, throughout the stream, or right at the end of urinating?
rationale: Localizes dysuria: initial suggests urethritis; terminal suggests trigonitis/cystitis.

text: On a scale from 1 to 10, how severe is the burning or stinging discomfort when passing urine?
rationale: Standardized clinical quantification of dysuria severity.

text: Do you feel a constant dull ache, fullness, or tenderness in your lower pelvic area right above the pubic bone?
rationale: Identifies acute cystitis bladder inflammation or pelvic floor spasm.

text: Have you noticed any white, yellow, green, or clear fluid discharge from the tip of your urethra?
rationale: Key diagnostic sign separating infectious urethritis (gonococcal/chlamydial) from cystitis.

text: Do you have aching discomfort in the perineum (between the scrotum/vagina and anus), particularly when sitting down?
rationale: Suggests acute or chronic prostatitis or pudendal nerve irritation.

text: Do you have any tenderness, swelling, or dragging discomfort in the testicles, scrotum, or groin crease?
rationale: Screens for epididymo-orchitis or referred renal colic.

text: Do you have pain in your mid-to-lower back or side, just under the ribcage?
rationale: Identifies costovertebral angle pain characteristic of pyelonephritis or obstructing stone.

text: Does the flank or back pain radiate downward into your groin, lower abdomen, or genital area?
rationale: Classic radiation pattern of acute ureteral colic as a stone migrates.

text: Do your urinary symptoms or burning tend to occur or flare up within 24 to 48 hours after sexual intercourse?
rationale: Characteristic pattern of honeymoon cystitis or post-coital irritation.

text: Does your bladder pain worsen when eating spicy foods, acidic citrus, artificial sweeteners, or drinking coffee?
rationale: Suggests interstitial cystitis / bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS).

text: Has your urine appeared cloudy, murky, or turbid rather than clear and translucent?
rationale: Suggests pyuria (white blood cells), bacteriuria, or precipitated crystal salts.

text: Have you noticed a particularly strong, pungent, or ammoniacal smell to your urine recently?
rationale: Indicates urea-splitting bacterial infection (e.g. Proteus) or concentrated urine.

text: Does your urine produce thick, persistent white foam or bubbles that linger in the toilet bowl?
rationale: Classic hallmark of significant proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome, or renal disease.

text: Has your urine ever looked dark brown like iced tea or cola?
rationale: Indicates glomerular bleeding (glomerulonephritis) or myoglobinuria from rhabdomyolysis.

text: Have you ever passed small hard gritty particles, gravel, or visible stones in your urine?
rationale: Direct confirmation of active nephrolithiasis or crystalluria.

text: Have you ever been diagnosed with kidney stones in the past, or had a procedure like lithotripsy to break one up?
rationale: Prior history carries a 50% recurrence rate within 5-10 years.

text: How many urinary tract infections (UTIs) have you had in the past 12 months?
rationale: Defines recurrent UTIs (>=2 in 6 months or >=3 in 12 months) requiring workup.

text: Did you have frequent kidney infections, bedwetting, or reflux surgery as a child?
rationale: Screens for congenital vesicoureteral reflux or renal scarring.

text: Approximately how many liters or glasses of water do you drink on a typical day?
rationale: Evaluates hydration deficit as a major reversible risk factor for stones and UTIs.

text: Have you had a urinary catheter, cystoscopy, or urological procedure within the past month?
rationale: Major risk factor for catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) or stricture.

text: Is your trouble starting to urinate noticeably worse right after waking up in the morning?
rationale: Evaluates overnight urinary stasis and circadian variation in BPH tone.

text: Does drinking caffeinated coffee or tea immediately trigger unbearable urinary urgency within 20 minutes?
rationale: Documents caffeine-induced detrusor hypersensitivity.

text: Have you ever tripped, slipped, or fallen while rushing out of bed to the bathroom in the dark?
rationale: High-priority geriatric safety and fracture risk assessment.

text: Do you feel sudden severe cramping contractions in your bladder that make you double over?
rationale: Identifies acute uninhibited detrusor contractions or catheter-induced spasms.

text: Can you physically feel a bulging, tender ball above your pubic bone after urinating?
rationale: Palpable bladder fullness diagnostic of significant post-void residual.

text: Do you consume high amounts of dairy, calcium supplements, or high-oxalate foods like spinach and nuts?
rationale: Nutritional metabolic stone risk assessment.

text: Does your pelvic or bladder pain temporarily feel relieved immediately after you empty your bladder?
rationale: Classic diagnostic hallmark of interstitial cystitis / bladder pain syndrome.

text: If you had prostate surgery, does urine leak continuously whenever you change positions?
rationale: Screens for post-prostatectomy stress urinary incontinence.

text: Have you ever taken a preventative single antibiotic pill immediately after sexual intercourse?
rationale: Evaluates established clinical management of post-coital recurrent cystitis.

text: When you have flank pain, do you pace the room unable to find any comfortable position to sit or lie?
rationale: Classic restless pacing characteristic of acute ureteral colic.

text: Have routine lab tests ever found microscopic blood in your urine that you could not see with your own eyes?
rationale: Screens for asymptomatic microscopic hematuria requiring AUA guidelines evaluation.

text: Have you taken daily high doses of aspirin, acetaminophen, or ibuprofen for months or years?
rationale: Screens for analgesic nephropathy and papillary necrosis.

text: Has anyone in your family had polycystic kidney disease (PKD), brain aneurysms, or early dialysis?
rationale: Screens for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).

text: Is your cough completely dry and hacking, or are you bringing up mucus and phlegm?
rationale: Differentiates dry bronchial irritation (ACE-inhibitors, viral, GERD) from productive infection.

text: What color is the phlegm: clear, milky white, yellow, green, or rust-colored?
rationale: Assesses neutrophilic purulence indicative of bacterial infection versus mucoid asthma/allergy.

text: How much phlegm are you producing each day: a few teaspoonfuls, or more like a quarter to half a cup?
rationale: Large volume purulent sputum suggests bronchiectasis, lung abscess, or chronic bronchitis.

text: Does your cough wake you up during the night or is it worst first thing in the morning upon standing?
rationale: Nighttime cough suggests cough-variant asthma or GERD; morning cough suggests chronic bronchitis.

text: Do you feel mucus constantly dripping down the back of your throat, causing you to clear your throat?
rationale: Identifies upper airway cough syndrome (post-nasal drip) from rhinosinusitis.

text: How many flights of stairs or how many flat blocks can you walk before having to stop and catch your breath?
rationale: Objective mMRC functional dyspnea staging.

text: Are you feeling out of breath even when sitting completely still, or when trying to speak a full sentence?
rationale: Signals severe physiological respiratory compromise.

text: Do you have to prop yourself up on two or more pillows at night to avoid feeling suffocated?
rationale: Classic hallmark of elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure in congestive heart failure.

text: Have you ever woken up abruptly 1-2 hours after falling asleep gasping for air and had to sit by an open window?
rationale: Classic description of Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea (PND).

text: Do you hear an audible whistling or squeaking sound when you breathe out?
rationale: Direct clinical marker of small airway bronchospasm seen in asthma and COPD.

text: Do you hear a harsh, high-pitched crowing sound in your neck when breathing in?
rationale: Signals life-threatening upper airway / laryngeal obstruction (stridor).

text: Does your chest pain feel sharp and catch like a knife specifically when you take a deep breath or cough?
rationale: Differentiates pleurisy (pneumonia, PE, pleuritis) from myocardial ischemia.

text: Have you had a measured high fever with shaking chills that make your teeth chatter?
rationale: Strong indicator of consolidated lobar pneumonia or systemic bacteremia.

text: Have you been having drenching night sweats that require changing your pajamas or bedsheets?
rationale: Classic B-symptom of tuberculosis, lymphoma, or chronic pulmonary mycobacterial infection.

text: Have you ever smoked cigarettes, cigars, or vaped, and for approximately how many pack-years?
rationale: Determines cumulative pack-year history for COPD and bronchogenic carcinoma risk.

text: Have you worked around asbestos, silica, mining, grain silos, chemical fumes, or sandblasting?
rationale: Screens for occupational pneumoconiosis, silicosis, and malignant mesothelioma.

text: Did you have asthma, eczema, or severe hay fever during your childhood or adolescence?
rationale: Establishes atopic march and allergic airway hyperresponsiveness.

text: Do you currently use rescue inhalers like albuterol, and how many times per week do you need them?
rationale: Measures asthma/COPD control (rescue use >2 times/week indicates uncontrolled disease).

text: Have you taken a long flight or car ride over 4 hours, or had surgery or leg cast in the past month?
rationale: Critical Virchow's triad risk factor for deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.

text: Have you lost weight unexpectedly without trying while experiencing this cough or shortness of breath?
rationale: Red-flag constitutional symptom of pulmonary malignancy or chronic tuberculosis.

text: Does breathing in cold winter air or stepping into an air-conditioned room trigger a coughing fit?
rationale: Classic sign of nonspecific bronchial hyperresponsiveness.

text: Does your chest start wheezing or tightening up 10-15 minutes into vigorous exercise?
rationale: Hallmark of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB).

text: Do you get severe asthma flare-ups, wheezing, or facial flushing after taking aspirin or ibuprofen?
rationale: Samter's Triad (Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease: asthma, nasal polyps, ASA sensitivity).

text: Does your chronic cough worsen when lying down flat after dinner, accompanied by a sour taste in your throat?
rationale: GERD-induced chronic cough mediated by vagal esophagobronchial reflex.

text: Do you keep pet birds, pigeons, or down feather pillows/quilts at home?
rationale: Screens for Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis (bird fancier's lung).

text: Has there been visible black mold, water leaks, or musty damp odors in your home or workplace?
rationale: Identifies environmental mold-induced allergic fungal airway disease.

text: Does your throat feel constantly raw, dry, or irritated despite drinking plenty of liquids?
rationale: Screens for chronic laryngeal sensory neuropathy or reflux laryngitis.

text: Have you ever coughed so hard that you became dizzy, saw stars, or momentarily passed out?
rationale: Cough syncope: transient cerebral hypoperfusion during prolonged high-pressure Valsalva cough.

text: Can you reproduce your sharp chest pain by pressing with your fingers on the joints between your ribs and breastbone?
rationale: Confirms costochondritis (Tietze syndrome) as a benign musculoskeletal chest pain etiology.

text: Have you experienced severe breathlessness or headache when traveling to mountain elevations above 8,000 feet?
rationale: Screens for high altitude pulmonary or cerebral edema susceptibility.

text: Has your partner heard you snore loudly, snort, or stop breathing during sleep?
rationale: Screens for obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.

text: Do you wake up in the morning with dull throbbing headaches that wear off after an hour?
rationale: Classic sign of nocturnal hypercapnia and hypoventilation.

text: Do you have chronic pressure in your forehead and cheekbones with thick discolored nasal drainage?
rationale: Identifies chronic rhinosinusitis contributing to lower airway inflammation.

text: Have you ever had nasal polyps diagnosed or surgically removed from your sinuses?
rationale: Associated with eosinophilic asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis.

text: Have you brought up thick mucus every single day for over a year?
rationale: Hallmark feature of bronchiectasis.

text: Does the chest sensation feel like a heavy weight, squeezing pressure, fullness, or tight band around your chest?
rationale: Classic visceral angina characterization typical of myocardial ischemia.

text: Does the discomfort radiate into your left shoulder, down your arm, or up into your neck, throat, or lower jaw?
rationale: Classic dermatomal radiation of cardiac pain (T1-T4 spinal segments).

text: Does the chest discomfort consistently come on when walking, climbing stairs, carrying groceries, or in cold weather?
rationale: Defines exertional angina pectoris due to fixed coronary stenosis.

text: Does the chest tightness go away completely within 5 to 10 minutes when you stop moving and sit down to rest?
rationale: Key diagnostic criterion for stable exertional angina.

text: If you have sublingual nitroglycerin, does placing one tablet under your tongue relieve the discomfort within 3 to 5 minutes?
rationale: Supports vascular smooth muscle dilation of coronary vasculature in ischemia.

text: Is the chest pain sharp and does it get significantly worse when lying flat on your back, but improve when leaning forward?
rationale: Classic diagnostic feature of acute pericarditis.

text: Does your heart feel like it is racing at 150+ beats per minute, or does it feel like occasional skipped or extra beats?
rationale: Differentiates sustained tachyarrhythmias (SVT, AFib) from benign PVCs/PACs.

text: Do these racing heart episodes start and stop abruptly like flipping an electric light switch?
rationale: Hallmark of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT) or paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

text: Have you actually blacked out, lost consciousness, or collapsed to the floor during an episode?
rationale: High-risk cardiac syncope screen indicating ventricular tachycardia, high-grade AV block, or severe aortic stenosis.

text: Do you feel intensely dizzy or like the world is going gray when you stand up quickly from a bed or chair?
rationale: Evaluates orthostatic hypotension, volume depletion, or autonomic neuropathy.

text: Is the leg swelling present in both legs equally, and does it worsen progressively toward the evening?
rationale: Symmetric dependent edema indicates systemic volume overload (CHF, cirrhosis, renal failure).

text: If you press your thumb firmly against your shin bone for 5 seconds, does an indentation stay behind?
rationale: Objectively confirms pitting peripheral edema.

text: Do you experience cramping pain in your calves or thighs when walking a predictable distance that stops when you pause?
rationale: Classic symptom of peripheral arterial disease (intermittent claudication).

text: Is one calf visibly swollen, warm, red, or tender compared to the other leg?
rationale: Screen for unilateral Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT).

text: Have you been diagnosed with high blood pressure, and what are your typical systolic and diastolic numbers at home?
rationale: Assesses chronic cardiovascular risk and hypertensive urgency.

text: Have you been told your cholesterol or LDL is elevated, and do you take a cholesterol-lowering medication like a statin?
rationale: Key modifiable atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk factor.

text: Have you ever had a heart attack, coronary stent placed, or coronary bypass (CABG) surgery in the past?
rationale: Extremely high pre-test probability for secondary coronary events.

text: Did any parent, brother, or sister have a heart attack or cardiac arrest before age 55 in men or 65 in women?
rationale: Independent major risk factor for familial hypercholesterolemia and premature CAD.

text: Do you have diabetes? (In diabetic patients, cardiac ischemia may present without chest pain, causing only breathlessness or nausea)
rationale: Critical clinical caveat for atypical / silent myocardial infarction in diabetics.

text: Have you used cocaine, amphetamines, energy pills, or prescription stimulants recently?
rationale: Potent cause of coronary vasospasm, myocardial infarction, and acute aortic dissection.

text: Can you walk across a level grocery store without needing to pause for chest tightness?
rationale: Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) Functional Angina Class II/III assessment.

text: Does severe emotional upset, frustration, or anger trigger the pressure in your chest?
rationale: Stress-induced coronary vasospasm or supply-demand mismatch ischemia.

text: Does chest discomfort strike more easily if you go for a walk immediately after eating a large, heavy meal?
rationale: Postprandial angina from splanchnic blood pooling and increased myocardial workload.

text: Can you stop your racing heart episodes by holding your breath and bearing down (Valsalva) or splashing ice water on your face?
rationale: Classic clinical differentiator of AV nodal re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT).

text: Does drinking an extra cup of espresso, energy drink, or dark chocolate provoke noticeable heart thumps?
rationale: Documents sympathomimetic adrenergic ectopy.

text: Do you get chest pain when lying flat at night that forces you to sit upright?
rationale: Angina decubitus: increased venous return overloading the failing ischemic ventricle.

text: Does your ankle swelling noticeably shrink back down to normal by morning after elevating your legs overnight?
rationale: Confirms dependent venous stasis rather than non-pitting lymphedema.

text: Does foot or toe pain wake you up at night, and does hanging your foot over the edge of the bed relieve it?
rationale: Hallmark of critical limb ischemia (Fontaine stage III) in severe peripheral arterial disease.

text: Have you noticed generalized muscle soreness, stiffness, or weakness since starting your cholesterol medication?
rationale: Screens for statin-associated muscle symptoms (SAMS) and myopathy.

text: Have you ever been told you have a heart murmur, leaky heart valve, or mitral valve prolapse?
rationale: Assesses valvular heart disease and endocarditis risk.

text: Did you have rheumatic fever, chorea, or scarlet fever as a child?
rationale: Major risk factor for late rheumatic mitral stenosis.

text: Have you ever been diagnosed with Atrial Fibrillation (AFib) or flutter?
rationale: Determines CHA2DS2-VASc stroke risk and anticoagulation indication.

text: Have you been told you have a bicuspid aortic valve or thoracic aortic enlargement?
rationale: Screens for ascending aortic aneurysm risk.

text: Are your feet and toes persistently icy cold and pale compared to the rest of your body?
rationale: Distal arterial hypoperfusion in peripheral arterial disease.

text: Is the pain located in the upper right side of your belly under the ribs, especially after eating fatty or greasy foods?
rationale: Suggests biliary colic, acute cholecystitis, or choledocholithiasis.

text: Is the discomfort a burning or gnawing ache high in the center of your belly that changes after meals or antacids?
rationale: Differentiates peptic ulcer disease and gastritis (duodenal improves with food; gastric worsens).

text: Did the pain begin around your belly button and then migrate over several hours down into your lower right belly?
rationale: Classic presentation of acute appendicitis.

text: Is the pain concentrated in your lower left abdomen accompanied by a fever or constipation?
rationale: Characteristic presentation of acute colonic diverticulitis.

text: Does the pain bore straight through into your mid-back, and do you feel better sitting forward with knees bent?
rationale: Classic hallmark of acute pancreatitis.

text: Do you have difficulty swallowing solids, liquids, or both, and does food feel stuck in your mid-chest?
rationale: Differentiates mechanical obstruction (cancer, stricture: solids first) from motility disorders (achalasia: solids and liquids).

text: Does it actively hurt when you swallow food or liquids (odynophagia)?
rationale: Suggests esophageal ulceration, candidiasis, or viral herpes/CMV esophagitis.

text: Do you get a burning sensation rising up behind your breastbone, or a sour, bitter liquid coming up into your mouth?
rationale: Hallmark of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).

text: Do you feel completely full after eating just a few bites of food, even when you sat down feeling hungry?
rationale: Concerning symptom for gastric outlet obstruction, gastroparesis, or gastric malignancy.

text: How many times have you vomited in the past 24 hours, and can you keep down sips of water?
rationale: Assesses hydration status and risk of hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.

text: Is the vomit bright green or dark yellow bile, indicating the stomach is empty and small bowel is regurgitating?
rationale: Confirms post-pyloric emesis, common in small bowel obstruction.

text: How many loose or liquid bowel movements are you having each day, and has this lasted more than 2 weeks?
rationale: Quantifies acute (<2 weeks) versus chronic (>4 weeks) diarrheal illness.

text: Does diarrhea ever wake you up from a sound sleep in the middle of the night?
rationale: Definitive marker of organic secretory or inflammatory bowel disease rather than functional IBS.

text: Have you noticed bright red blood coating the stool, dripping into the bowl, or on the toilet paper?
rationale: Hematochezia: indicates lower GI source (hemorrhoids, anal fissure, diverticular bleed, rectal cancer).

text: Have your bowel movements looked jet black, sticky, tarry, and had an overwhelmingly foul odor?
rationale: Melena: diagnostic of significant upper GI bleeding digested by gastric acid and bacteria.

text: Have your bowel movements looked abnormally pale, grayish-white, or clay-colored?
rationale: Pathognomonic sign of biliary ductal obstruction preventing bilirubin excretion.

text: Have your family or friends noticed a yellow tint to the whites of your eyes (sclera) or your skin?
rationale: Hyperbilirubinemia: signals hepatocellular injury, cholestasis, or hemolysis.

text: Have you had intense, widespread skin itching without any visible rash, especially on your palms and soles?
rationale: Hallmark of cholestatic jaundice with bile salt deposition in skin.

text: Have you lost significant weight without dieting while experiencing these digestive changes?
rationale: Critical red flag for gastrointestinal malignancy, celiac disease, or IBD.

text: When was your last screening colonoscopy, and have you ever had precancerous colon polyps removed?
rationale: Screens for colorectal cancer risk and surveillance compliance.

text: Do you sleep with the head of your bed elevated to prevent acid from backing up into your throat?
rationale: Standard lifestyle anti-reflux measure assessment.

text: Does eating fried chicken, pizza, or greasy food trigger upper abdominal pain 30 to 60 minutes later?
rationale: Evaluates postprandial gallbladder contraction against biliary stones.

text: Do you get severe gas, gurgling bloating, and watery diarrhea within an hour of drinking cow's milk or eating ice cream?
rationale: Identifies adult-onset lactase deficiency (lactose intolerance).

text: Do you experience chronic diarrhea, bloating, fatigue, or itchy blistering rashes after eating wheat or bread?
rationale: Screens for celiac disease and dermatitis herpetiformis.

text: Do you feel a painful, persistent sensation that you need to pass stool even when your rectum is completely empty?
rationale: Tenesmus: classic indicator of rectal inflammation (proctitis, ulcerative colitis, rectal mass).

text: Are your bowel movements typically hard, dry, separate small pellets that require severe straining to pass?
rationale: Bristol Stool Form Scale Type 1-2 indicating slow colonic transit constipation.

text: Did your loose watery diarrhea begin during or within a few weeks after taking a course of antibiotic pills?
rationale: Critical screen for Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) colitis.

text: Do you feel soft tissue protruding or popping out of your rectum when you strain, which has to be pushed back in?
rationale: Evaluates prolapsing internal hemorrhoids (Grade II-III).

text: Does passing a bowel movement feel intensely sharp like passing broken shards of glass, with a spot of bright blood on wiping?
rationale: Pathognomonic description of acute anal fissure.

text: Has your abdomen become noticeably distended or your belt size expanded even while your arms and legs look thinner?
rationale: Classic sign of abdominal ascites from portal hypertension or peritoneal carcinomatosis.

text: Do you have to take daily laxatives, senna, or enemas in order to have a bowel movement?
rationale: Evaluates laxative dependency and melanosis coli risk.

text: Do you struggle to control passing gas or experience occasional accidental stool staining?
rationale: Assesses anal sphincter integrity and fecal incontinence.

text: Does your lower belly cramping improve immediately after you pass a bowel movement, and worsen with life stress?
rationale: Rome IV diagnostic criteria for Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).

text: Do you get burning stomach aches after taking aspirin, Aleve, or Advil on an empty stomach?
rationale: Screens for NSAID-induced gastric mucosal injury.

text: Did the headache reach maximum, agonizing intensity within a matter of seconds (like a clap of thunder)?
rationale: Key discriminator for subarachnoid hemorrhage (thunderclap headache).

text: Is the headache pounding or throbbing on one side of your head, and does bright light or loud sound make it worse?
rationale: Classic migraine presentation with photophobia/phonophobia.

text: Is the headache most severe upon waking in the morning, and is it accompanied by sudden nausea or vomiting?
rationale: Classic red-flag presentation of increased intracranial pressure or intracranial mass.

text: Do you see shimmering zigzag lines, blind spots, or flashing lights in your vision 20 to 30 minutes before the headache starts?
rationale: Migraine visual aura caused by cortical spreading depression.

text: Is the weakness isolated to one arm, one leg, or one entire side of your body?
rationale: Focal pyramidal tract deficit typical of stroke or demyelinating lesion.

text: Do you have difficulty standing up from a low chair or lifting your arms above your head to comb your hair?
rationale: Characteristic proximal myopathy seen in polymyositis or steroid myopathy.

text: Do your toes catch on the floor or rug when you walk, causing you to trip (foot drop)?
rationale: Distal motor neuropathy involving the common peroneal nerve or L5 root.

text: Is the numbness in a stocking-and-glove pattern over both feet and hands, or along a single specific nerve stripe?
rationale: Differentiates length-dependent polyneuropathy from focal radiculopathy/entrapment.

text: Does your hand shake when resting in your lap, or does the shaking only appear when you reach for a cup?
rationale: Differentiates Parkinsonian resting tremor from essential action tremor.

text: Is your speech slurred like you are intoxicated, or are you having trouble getting your mouth muscles to form words?
rationale: Dysarthria: indicates brainstem, cerebellar, or cranial nerve motor deficit.

text: Do you know what you want to say but the words won't come out, or are you having trouble understanding what others say to you?
rationale: Expressive (Broca) or receptive (Wernicke) aphasia indicating cortical stroke.

text: Does the room literally spin around you like you stepped off a carnival ride, or do you feel lightheaded like you might faint?
rationale: Differentiates true vestibular vertigo from cardiovascular presyncope.

text: Does turning your head quickly to one side in bed trigger intense spinning that lasts under 60 seconds?
rationale: Pathognomonic description of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

text: Do you have ringing, roaring, or buzzing in one ear together with muffled hearing or fullness?
rationale: Screens for Meniere's disease, acoustic neuroma, or labyrinthitis.

text: Have you been uncoordinated, dropping utensils, or staggering like you are walking on an unstable ship?
rationale: Indicates cerebellar ataxia or dorsal column sensory ataxia.

text: Have you noticed one corner of your mouth drooping, and can you still wrinkle your forehead on that side?
rationale: Cranial nerve VII deficit: distinguishes upper motor neuron stroke from lower motor neuron Bell's palsy.

text: When you look with both eyes open, do you see two images side-by-side or stacked, which resolves when you close either eye?
rationale: Binocular diplopia: indicates ocular motor nerve palsy (CN III, IV, or VI).

text: Is your neck stiff to the point that you cannot touch your chin to your chest, especially with a fever?
rationale: Classic meningeal irritation sign (meningismus) in acute meningitis.

text: Have you been repeating the same questions, misplacing items in strange locations, or getting lost in familiar neighborhoods?
rationale: Evaluates cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, or progressive dementia.

text: Have you ever had an unprovoked seizure, convulsion, sudden collapse with shaking, or loss of time?
rationale: Establishes seizure disorder and post-ictal state.

text: Do your thumb, index, and middle fingers go numb and tingle at night, and do you shake your hand to wake it up?
rationale: Classic Phalen/Flick sign of median nerve entrapment at the carpal tunnel.

text: Do you feel an electric shock shooting down your spine into your legs when you bend your neck forward?
rationale: Lhermitte's sign: indicates cervical spinal cord demyelination or compression.

text: Does the shooting pain down your leg get sharply worse whenever you cough, sneeze, or strain on the toilet?
rationale: Confirms disc herniation nerve root compression exacerbated by increased thecal sac pressure.

text: Do you get an irresistible urge to move your legs in the evening accompanied by creepy-crawly sensations inside the calves?
rationale: Diagnostic criteria for Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS / Willis-Ekbom disease).

text: Have you had involuntary twitching or spasms of your eyelid or the corner of your mouth?
rationale: Screens for benign myokymia or hemifacial spasm.

text: Have you noticed a loss or significant blunting of your sense of smell or taste?
rationale: Early prodromal marker for Parkinson's disease or post-viral olfactory neuropathy.

text: Does going into a quiet, dark bedroom and falling asleep make your severe headache disappear?
rationale: Classic clinical feature of primary migraine headache termination.

text: Does washing your face, brushing your teeth, or cold wind blowing on your cheek trigger electric jolts of pain?
rationale: Diagnostic triggers of classic trigeminal neuralgia (tic douloureux).

text: Do your vision, walking, or fatigue symptoms get noticeably worse after taking a hot shower or in hot weather?
rationale: Uhthoff's phenomenon indicative of multiple sclerosis demyelinated nerve conduction block.

text: Do you drop coffee cups or stumble into doorways within the first 30 minutes of waking up?
rationale: Assesses morning motor coordination and cerebellar/vestibular latency.

text: Do you get excruciating stabbing pain strictly around one eye accompanied by eye tearing and a runny nostril?
rationale: Hallmark description of episodic or chronic cluster headache.

text: Does your headache feel like a tight rubber band or vice squeezing around your temples and forehead?
rationale: Classic presentation of tension-type headache.

text: Do you take triptans, Excedrin, or pain pills more than 10-15 days each month for headaches?
rationale: Identifies medication overuse (rebound) headache.

text: How long does morning stiffness last after waking up: under 30 minutes, or longer than an hour?
rationale: Stiffness >1 hr strongly indicates inflammatory arthritis (RA/ankylosing spondylitis); <30 min suggests OA.

text: Are the affected joints visibly swollen, spongy, hot to the touch, or red?
rationale: Hallmark of active joint effusion, synovitis, or crystalline/septic arthritis.

text: Does the pain affect the small joints of both hands symmetrically, or is it in large weight-bearing joints like the knee or hip?
rationale: Symmetric small joint: RA/Lupus; asymmetric large joint: Osteoarthritis or Spondyloarthritis.

text: Does your back pain shoot down through your buttock and down the back or side of your leg below the knee?
rationale: Radiculopathy: nerve root impingement (sciatica, disc herniation L4-S1).

text: Does your back pain wake you up in the second half of the night and actually improve once you get up and exercise?
rationale: Hallmark of inflammatory spondyloarthritis / ankylosing spondylitis.

text: Did agonizing, red, swollen pain strike your big toe joint in the middle of the night?
rationale: Classic podagra of acute gouty arthritis.

text: Do your fingers or toes turn stark white, then deep blue, and finally red and throbbing when exposed to cold?
rationale: Classic Raynaud's phenomenon associated with systemic sclerosis, lupus, or mixed connective tissue disease.

text: Have you had persistent dry gritty eyes and dry mouth requiring constant water sips for over 3 months?
rationale: Sicca complex indicative of primary Sjogren's syndrome.

text: Have you taken oral prednisone or steroid pills for long periods in the past?
rationale: Major risk factor for osteoporotic compression fractures and avascular necrosis of the femoral head.

text: Does your knee ever feel unstable or buckle/give way under you when walking or changing directions?
rationale: Cruciate ligament (ACL/PCL) instability or patellar subluxation.

text: Does your knee joint ever physically lock in place so that you cannot bend or straighten it until you wiggle it?
rationale: Mechanical locking characteristic of a bucket-handle meniscal tear or loose body.

text: Does your shoulder hurt when reaching up into a high cabinet, combing your hair, or putting on a coat?
rationale: Classic subacromial impingement or rotator cuff tendinopathy.

text: Does severe shoulder pain wake you up when you roll onto that side at night?
rationale: Hallmark of rotator cuff tears and adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder).

text: Is your hip pain felt deeply in the front of your groin crease when putting on your socks or walking?
rationale: True hip joint pathology (osteoarthritis) is localized to the groin, not the lateral hip.

text: Is the pain located on the outer bony point of your hip, and is it very tender to press on with your fingers?
rationale: Classic greater trochanteric pain syndrome (trochanteric bursitis / gluteal tendinopathy).

text: Is heel pain intensely sharp on the very first few steps when getting out of bed in the morning, then loosens up?
rationale: Pathognomonic presentation of acute plantar fasciitis.

text: Do you have tenderness, stiffness, or a nodular swelling at the back of your heel on the Achilles tendon?
rationale: Screens for insertional or non-insertional Achilles tendinopathy.

text: Does a finger catch, pop, or get stuck in a curled position when you close your fist?
rationale: Stenosing tenosynovitis (trigger finger) involving the A1 pulley.

text: Does it hurt on the outside bump of your elbow when gripping a heavy coffee mug or turning a doorknob?
rationale: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) of the extensor carpi radialis brevis tendon.

text: Does moving your thumb or making a fist hurt sharply on the thumb side of your wrist?
rationale: De Quervain's tenosynovitis of the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis.

text: Does turning your neck to the side cause sharp pain or tingling to shoot down into your arm or fingers?
rationale: Spurling's sign indicating cervical nerve root radiculopathy.

text: Does lower back and leg heaviness improve when you lean forward over a grocery shopping cart or sit down?
rationale: Neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal canal stenosis.

text: Do you have widespread pain all over your body accompanied by unrefreshing sleep, brain fog, and chronic fatigue?
rationale: ACR criteria for fibromyalgia syndrome.

text: Are you over age 50 and experiencing sudden severe aching and stiffness in both shoulders, neck, and pelvic girdle?
rationale: Classic presentation of Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR).

text: Do you feel a tight, bulging fullness behind your knee that makes it difficult to fully bend your leg?
rationale: Popliteal (Baker's) cyst secondary to knee effusion.

text: Does your kneecap ache when sitting with bent knees for long movies or car rides, or when walking down stairs?
rationale: Movie-goer's sign in patellofemoral pain syndrome.

text: Can you easily bend your thumbs back to touch your forearms, or have you been double-jointed all your life?
rationale: Beighton score assessment for Ehlers-Danlos or hypermobility spectrum disorder.

text: Has your vision become blurry, foggy, or completely dark in the affected eye?
rationale: Quantifies acute visual acuity loss.

text: Do you see brief arcs or flashes of light like lightning bolts in the corner of your vision, especially in the dark?
rationale: Photopsia: indicates mechanical traction of the vitreous on the retina.

text: Have you noticed a sudden shower of new dark spots, cobwebs, or floating specks drifting across your vision?
rationale: Classic symptom of acute posterior vitreous detachment or vitreous hemorrhage.

text: Does it look like a dark curtain, veil, or shadow is creeping in from the top, bottom, or side of your vision?
rationale: Pathognomonic symptom of advancing retinal detachment.

text: Does it hurt deeply in the back of your eye socket specifically when you look up, down, or sideways?
rationale: Classic sign of optic neuritis (strongly associated with multiple sclerosis).

text: Do you have severe, boring eye and brow pain with nausea and rainbow-colored halos around streetlights?
rationale: Classic presentation of acute angle-closure glaucoma from dangerous intraocular pressure spike.

text: Is your eye bloodshot with thick yellow or green crusting that glues your eyelids shut in the morning?
rationale: Diagnostic of acute bacterial conjunctivitis.

text: Are both eyes watery, intensely itchy, and accompanied by sneezing or a runny nose?
rationale: Classic presentation of allergic conjunctivitis.

text: Does indoor room light or sunlight cause unbearable squinting or eye pain?
rationale: Indicates anterior uveitis (iritis) or corneal ulceration.

text: Does it feel like there is sand, grit, or a piece of glass stuck under your eyelid every time you blink?
rationale: Classic sign of corneal abrasion, subtarsal foreign body, or severe dry eye.

text: Do you wear soft or hard contact lenses, and have you ever slept in them or washed them with tap water?
rationale: Major risk factor for rapidly progressive Pseudomonas or Acanthamoeba keratitis.

text: Did any cleaning fluid, acid, alkali, battery fluid, or chemical splash into your eye?
rationale: Ophthalmic chemical emergency requiring immediate, copious irrigation.

text: Have you had cataract surgery, LASIK, glaucoma procedures, or retinal laser treatment in the past?
rationale: Important surgical context for postoperative endophthalmitis or retinal tear.

text: Do your eyes feel gritty, burning, and red by afternoon, and does blinking or using lubricating eye drops help?
rationale: Classic evaporative or aqueous-deficient dry eye disease.

text: Do oncoming car headlights at night cause starbursts, blinding glare, or halos that make night driving difficult?
rationale: Classic symptom of developing nuclear sclerotic or cortical cataracts.

text: Do you find yourself having to hold books, menus, or your smartphone farther away at arm's length to read small print?
rationale: Universal age-related presbyopia from crystalline lens elasticity loss.

text: Do straight doorframes or tile lines look wavy, bent, or distorted when looking with one eye at a time?
rationale: Metamorphopsia: pathognomonic symptom of macular degeneration or epiretinal membrane.

text: Do your eyelashes have greasy flakes or dandruff-like crusts along the eyelid margins in the morning?
rationale: Identifies anterior blepharitis and meibomian gland dysfunction.

text: Has one upper eyelid started drooping downward over your pupil, especially late in the day when tired?
rationale: Screens for myasthenia gravis (fatigable ptosis) or third nerve palsy.

text: Does one eye tear up constantly and spill water onto your cheek even when you are not crying or in wind?
rationale: Screens for nasolacrimal duct obstruction or punctal stenosis.

text: Do you get severe eye fatigue, temple aches, or brow strain after working on computer screens for several hours?
rationale: Screens for computer vision syndrome, uncorrected astigmatism, or accommodative spasm.

text: Do you have a firm, localized tender lump or pimple on your upper or lower eyelid margin?
rationale: Differentiates external hordeolum (stye) from chronic non-tender chalazion.

text: Is there a bright blood-red patch on the white of your eye with zero pain, zero discharge, and normal vision?
rationale: Classic benign subconjunctival hemorrhage after coughing, sneezing, or straining.

text: Is there a permanent dark, blurry smudge or blind spot right in the exact center of your visual focus?
rationale: Hallmark of macular disease (wet/dry AMD or macular hole).

text: Does cold water or hot coffee trigger a sharp zing that lingers for more than 10-15 seconds after you swallow?
rationale: Differentiates reversible pulpitis (<5 sec) from irreversible pulpitis (>10 sec linger).

text: Does it throb or hurt sharply every time you bite down or tap on that specific tooth?
rationale: Indicates acute apical periodontitis or cracked tooth syndrome.

text: Do you have a localized pimple, gum boil, or swelling on the gum tissue near the painful tooth?
rationale: Classic presentation of a localized periapical or periodontal abscess.

text: Has the swelling spread into your cheek, upper lip, or underneath your jawbone?
rationale: Signals spread of odontogenic infection into fascial spaces requiring systemic antibiotics and drainage.

text: Can you comfortably open your mouth wide enough to fit three fingers vertically between your front teeth?
rationale: Trismus (<35mm opening): indicates pterygomandibular space infection or peritonsillar abscess.

text: Do you have painful shallow ulcers inside your cheeks or lips with a red border and white center?
rationale: Screens for recurrent aphthous stomatitis or viral ulcerations.

text: Have you noticed a white patch (leukoplakia) or red velvety patch (erythroplakia) in your mouth that hasn't healed in 3 weeks?
rationale: High-risk screen for oral squamous cell carcinoma.

text: Does your mouth feel constantly dry like cotton, making it hard to swallow dry crackers without drinking water?
rationale: Identifies xerostomia from medications, radiation, or Sjogren's syndrome.

text: Do you have sharp pain in your ear even though the dentist says the problem is a lower back molar?
rationale: Referred otalgia via the auriculotemporal nerve from lower molar pathology or TMJ.

text: Do your gums regularly bleed when you floss between your teeth or brush with a soft toothbrush?
rationale: Direct clinical sign of active gingivitis or periodontal inflammation.

text: Can you feel any of your adult teeth wiggling or shifting position when you bite or chew?
rationale: Indicates advanced alveolar bone loss from severe periodontitis.

text: Have you or family members noticed persistent foul breath that doesn't go away after brushing or mouthwash?
rationale: Chronic halitosis: screens for deep periodontal pockets, tongue dorsum biofilm, or tonsilloliths.

text: Does your jaw joint click, pop, or grind when you open wide to yawn or chew hard food?
rationale: Temporomandibular Joint (TMJ) internal derangement or disc displacement.

text: Do you wake up with tired sore jaw muscles or temple headaches, or has a partner heard you grinding teeth at night?
rationale: Identifies nocturnal bruxism and excessive occlusal wear.

text: Does your tongue, lips, or roof of your mouth feel like it has been scalded by hot soup, with no visible rash?
rationale: Classic Burning Mouth Syndrome (glossodynia) or vitamin B12 deficiency.

text: Does dental floss consistently catch, shred, or snap when you try to clean between two specific teeth?
rationale: Indicates interproximal dental caries, defective overhanging filling, or calculus.

text: Does your tongue have a thick white curd-like coating that scrapes off with a brush, leaving raw red tissue?
rationale: Pathognomonic description of oral candidiasis (thrush).

text: If you wear full or partial dentures, have they become loose, causing sore spots or difficulty chewing?
rationale: Evaluates denture fit and progressive alveolar ridge resorption.

text: Is there swollen, painful gum tissue covering a partially erupted back wisdom tooth?
rationale: Pericoronitis of partially impacted third molar.

text: Does a lump swell up painfully under your jaw or in front of your ear whenever you smell or eat sour food?
rationale: Sialolithiasis (salivary gland stone obstruction of Wharton's or Stensen's duct).

text: Do you cough up foul-smelling small white chalky pebbles from the crevices of your tonsils?
rationale: Benign tonsilloliths (tonsil stones).

text: Do you have a mole or dark spot where one half does not look like the other half?
rationale: ABCDE melanoma criteria: Asymmetry.

text: Are the edges of any dark spot irregular, ragged, notched, or blurred?
rationale: ABCDE melanoma criteria: Border irregularity.

text: Does a mole contain multiple different shades of brown, black, red, white, or blue within the same spot?
rationale: ABCDE melanoma criteria: Color variegation.

text: Is any new or changing mole larger in diameter than a pencil eraser (greater than 6 millimeters)?
rationale: ABCDE melanoma criteria: Diameter.

text: Has a mole been visibly changing in size, shape, color, or has it started itching, oozing, or bleeding?
rationale: ABCDE melanoma criteria: Evolving (most sensitive criteria for melanoma).

text: Is your skin rash intensely itchy, especially at night when you get warm under the covers?
rationale: Screens for scabies, atopic eczema, or lichen planus.

text: Does your skin rash appear predominantly on areas exposed to sunlight (face, neck, forearms)?
rationale: Screens for photodermatitis, drug-induced photosensitivity, or systemic lupus malar rash.

text: Have you noticed an expanding red circular rash with a central clear area (bullseye rash) after spending time outdoors?
rationale: Erythema migrans: pathognomonic for early localized Lyme disease.

text: Do you get raised, itchy red welts (hives) that appear suddenly, last a few hours, and disappear without leaving a scar?
rationale: Classic presentation of acute or chronic urticaria.

text: Do the palms of your hands or fingers get painful cracks, fissures, and peeling skin in cold dry weather?
rationale: Irritant or allergic contact dermatitis / xerotic eczema.

text: Do you have a painful, burning strip of small fluid-filled blisters strictly limited to one side of your chest, back, or face?
rationale: Classic dermatomal presentation of Herpes Zoster (Shingles).

text: Do you have thick red patches covered with dry silvery-white scales on your elbows, knees, or scalp?
rationale: Pathognomonic description of chronic plaque psoriasis.

text: Have smooth, round, completely bald coin-sized spots appeared suddenly on your scalp or beard?
rationale: Screens for alopecia areata or autoimmune hair follicle destruction.

text: Do you have deep painful nodules or cysts on your jawline, chest, or back that leave permanent pitted scars?
rationale: Severe nodulocystic acne requiring systemic retinoid evaluation.

text: Have your toenails become thick, brittle, crumbly, and yellow or brownish-black?
rationale: Onychomycosis (fungal nail infection).

text: Do you have hundreds of tiny pinpoint red or purple spots on your lower legs that do not turn white when pressed?
rationale: Non-blanching petechiae indicative of thrombocytopenia or vasculitis.

text: Are your lower calves discolored with dark rusty-brown skin staining, itching, and swelling?
rationale: Stasis dermatitis and hemosiderin deposition from chronic venous insufficiency.

text: Do you have red, raw, burning skin folds under your breasts, groin, or belly that smell sour?
rationale: Intertrigo with secondary Candida infection.

text: Do you have a shiny, pearly bump on your nose or face with tiny visible blood vessels that bleeds easily?
rationale: Classic description of nodular basal cell carcinoma.

text: Are you having to drink massive amounts of water throughout the day and urinating enormous volumes every hour?
rationale: Classic triad of diabetes mellitus or diabetes insipidus.

text: Do you feel uncomfortably hot and sweat profusely when everyone else in the room feels completely comfortable?
rationale: Classic hyperthyroid metabolic hyperactivity symptom.

text: Are you constantly bundled up in sweaters and shivering when others are fine, with sluggish bowels and dry skin?
rationale: Classic hypothyroid metabolic slowing symptom.

text: Do you get jittery, sweaty, shaky, irritable, and lightheaded if your meals are delayed by an hour?
rationale: Screens for reactive or fasting hypoglycemia.
